variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen a company fail.
variants.body:
A company has gone under in {colony}. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

Workers are not an incidental detail in the politics of business failure. Labour should keep ordinary lives in view without inventing a dismissal or an unpaid wage. Solidarity requires attention to people, and a careful account should not claim to know their particular circumstances merely because a company has gone under.

We judge {target} critically. Business failure deserves more than a shrug, and the standards of stewardship should be examined rather than dismissed as irrelevant once an enterprise has gone under. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
